from manim import *
import os

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Golden Rule: Prerequisite Refresh", [
            "Exponents define a growth relationship.",
            "Base 'b' is the growth rate.",
            "Time 'x' determines total growth."
        ])
        
        # Asset path
        asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        eq = MathTex("x^n", "\\cdot", "x^m", "=", "x^{n+m}")
        eq.set_color(WHITE)
        # Apply layout fixes from issues
        self.place_at_grid(eq, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Use SVGMobject for SVGs, ImageMobject for actual raster images
        icon = SVGMobject(asset_path) if (os.path.exists(asset_path) and asset_path.endswith(".svg")) else Dot(color=BLACK)
        self.place_at_grid(icon, "B2", scale_factor=0.5)

        self.play(Write(eq), FadeIn(icon))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight x, n, m
        x_parts = eq.get_parts_by_tex("x")
        n_part = eq.get_part_by_tex("n")
        m_part = eq.get_part_by_tex("m")
        
        self.play(
            x_parts.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            n_part.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            m_part.animate.set_color("#00FF00")
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate summation visually
        n_m_sum = eq.get_part_by_tex("n+m")
        # Apply fix for yellow highlight box size
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(n_m_sum, color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(highlight_box, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=1.1)
        
        icon2 = SVGMobject(asset_path) if (os.path.exists(asset_path) and asset_path.endswith(".svg")) else Dot(color=BLACK)
        self.place_at_grid(icon2, "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(highlight_box), FadeIn(icon2))
        self.play(Flash(n_m_sum, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Powers as Fractional Indices", [
            "Roots are just fractional exponents.",
            "Square root is power of one-half.",
            "Cube root is power of one-third."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display root symbol as power x^{1/n}
        root_formula = MathTex(r"\sqrt[n]{x} = x^{1/n}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(root_formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(root_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Convert radical notation to fractional exponent notation (square root)
        sq_root = MathTex(r"\sqrt{x}", color=WHITE)
        sq_exp = MathTex(r"x^{1/2}", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sq_root, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(sq_root))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Transform(sq_root, sq_exp))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Cube root: ∛8 = 8^(1/3) = 2
        cube_root = MathTex(r"\sqrt[3]{8}", color=WHITE)
        cube_exp = MathTex(r"8^{1/3} = 2", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_root, 'F4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(cube_root))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Transform(cube_root, cube_exp))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Logarithms: The 'Reverse' Perspective", [
            "Logarithms find the missing time.",
            "They reverse the exponential process.",
            "Logarithms calculate the needed exponent."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_EXP = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        COLOR_LOG = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue

        # Math Objects
        exp_form = MathTex("y = b^x", color=COLOR_EXP)
        log_form = MathTex("\\log_{b}(y) = x", color=COLOR_LOG)
        
        # Asset Loading
        calc_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg")
        clock_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/clock.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show exponential form y = b^x
        self.place_in_area(exp_form, 'B3', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(calc_icon, 'B6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(exp_form), FadeIn(calc_icon))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_EXP)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate log conversion: log_b(y) = x
        self.place_in_area(log_form, 'D3', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(log_form))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_LOG)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Use arrows and icon to show movement
        arrow_animation = Arrow(start=exp_form.get_bottom(), end=log_form.get_top(), color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow_animation, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(clock_icon, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_animation), FadeIn(clock_icon))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Transformation Triangle", [
            "Exponents, logs, roots are linked.",
            "They rearrange three fixed numbers.",
            "These are inverse operations."
        ])
        
        # Triangle nodes
        exp_node = Text("Exponential\n(b^x = y)", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        log_node = Text("Logarithmic\n(log_b y = x)", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        root_node = Text("Roots/Inverse\n(y^(1/x) = b)", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        
        # Optimized positions based on constraints (columns 4-6)
        self.place_at_grid(exp_node, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(log_node, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(root_node, 'D6', scale_factor=0.8)

        tri = Polygon(
            self.grid['B5'], self.grid['D4'], self.grid['D6'],
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        # Arrows 
        arrow1 = Arrow(self.grid['B5'], self.grid['D4'], color=YELLOW, buff=0.5)
        arrow2 = Arrow(self.grid['D4'], self.grid['D6'], color=YELLOW, buff=0.5)
        arrow3 = Arrow(self.grid['D6'], self.grid['B5'], color=YELLOW, buff=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(tri), FadeIn(exp_node), FadeIn(log_node), FadeIn(root_node))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2), Create(arrow3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Rotate(VGroup(tri, exp_node, log_node, root_node, arrow1, arrow2, arrow3), angle=PI/3, about_point=np.array([2.5, 0, 0])))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Unified Language of Exponents, Roots, and Logarithms

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Prerequisite Refresh
sections.content: Briefly revisit the 'Exponential Identity' (b^x = y). Visualize a tree growing: the base 'b' is the growth rate, 'x' is time, and 'y' is the total height. Everything flows from this single relationship.
sections.example: If 2^3 = 8, the base is 2, the power is 3, and the result is 8.

sections.title: Powers as Fractional Indices
sections.content: Introduce the 'Fractional Power' notation. Explain that roots are simply exponents that are less than 1. Visually transform a square root symbol (√) into a power of 1/2 using a morphing animation.
sections.example: Visual transition: '√x' morphs into 'x^(1/2)'. For a cubic root, '∛8' becomes '8^(1/3) = 2'.

sections.title: Logarithms: The 'Reverse' Perspective
sections.content: Introduce logarithms as the notation for finding the *missing time* (exponent). Use an animation of a rabbit population: if the population hits a target size, log calculates how long it took to get there.
sections.example: The equation 2^x = 16 becomes log₂16 = 4. The log asks: 'To what power must I raise 2 to get 16?'

sections.title: The Transformation Triangle
sections.content: Present the 'Math Triangle' animation showing how b^x=y, log_b(y)=x, and y^(1/x)=b are just different ways to look at the same three numbers. This helps students map the parts of the equation to different roles.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Decibel Scale
sections.content: Show a sound meter. Explain that loudness is measured using log scales because the range of human hearing is massive. Connect back to the exponential growth of sound waves.
sections.example: A rock concert (100 dB) is 10^10 times more intense than a whisper (0 dB). Using logs simplifies 10,000,000,000 to just 10!
